name: Miswak Sticks (Salvadora persica)
description: Twigs from the Salvadora persica tree containing natural antimicrobials, silica, fluoride, and tannins — WHO-recognized as an effective oral hygiene tool with zero plastic waste.
chemicalName: Salvadora persica root and stem fibers
appearance: Pale tan-to-brown fibrous twig, ~15–20 cm long and ~5–8 mm diameter; bark scraped at one end to expose chewable wood that splays into bristles
chemistry: Active compounds: benzyl isothiocyanate (broad-spectrum antimicrobial vs S. mutans and P. gingivalis), salvadorine alkaloid, tannic acid (astringent that reduces gingival bleeding), silica (mild abrasive, RDA ~50–70), trace fluoride (~8–22 ppm), and sulfur compounds. Synergistic plaque/biofilm reduction without surfactants.
warnings: Trim the chewed end every 2–3 days to refresh fibers and avoid bacterial buildup. Excessive force damages enamel — let the bristles do the work, do not scrub. Source from reputable suppliers; sticks from polluted or chemically-treated trees may carry contaminants.
costNote: $1–3 per stick in bulk packs; single vacuum-sealed sticks $3–5
shelfLife: Vacuum-sealed: 1–2 years. Opened and dry-stored: several months. Active stick (in use): 1–2 weeks before fibers degrade
